data.narrative:
eGenesis, a Series C-stage biotech company founded by Luhan Yang and George Church, has raised $250M+ to date. Valuation analysis draws on a peer set of 3 same-stage private companies in Biotech & Health (Colossal Biosciences, Chai Discovery, New Limit) and 3 public comparables (RXRX, TEM, ONT.L).

Two methods triangulate valuation. Stage-progression analysis applies a 1.7x step-up multiplier to the $250M total raised proxy, implying $425M. Peer-median analysis across the 3 same-sector, same-stage private comparables yields a median valuation of $3.8B, with a range spanning $3.1B to $10.3B. Public-comp anchoring (P/S median: 8.1x across biotech tickers) cannot be applied due to absence of target revenue disclosure, typical for private companies. 

The two applicable methods produce a triangulated range of $361M (low) to $4.4B (high), with a median of $2.1B. The wide spread reflects material dispersion in the peer cohort—Colossal Biosciences trades at $10.3B while New Limit sits at $3.1B—and the tension between backward-looking capital-raised metrics and forward market comparables. Key uncertainties include platform differentiation relative to peers, clinical-stage risk, and whether disclosed valuations for high-end peers reflect recent financing or secondary activity.
